newsitem.title: USA: GulfWest Oil proven reserves increase.
newsitem.headline: GulfWest Oil proven reserves increase.

text.p: GulfWest Oil Co said Monday its proven oil and gas reserves increased 470 percent in 1996 due to its acquisition and development program, which is concentrated primarily in West Texas.
It said the present value of proved oil and gas reserves, using Securities and Exchange Commission guidelines, was $40 million, up from $7 million for 1995.
Gross revenues for 1996 increased to $2 million from $700,000 for 1995, it said.
The company said its daily production increased to 1,000 barrels from 133 barrels, and the number of owned and operated producing wells increased to 418 from 23.
It reported a working interest in over 14,000 developed acres, up from 5,000 at the close of 1995.

Marshall Smith, president and chief executive officer, said the company intends to continue its aggressive acquisition program and is currently evaluating and negotiating the purchase of an additional $20 million of producing properties with enhancement and development potential.

GulfWest is an independent oil and gas company focused primarily on the acquisition of producing properties with proved reserves that contain the potential for increased value through development and enhancement.
